content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using the [product_name] app for Android to show a simple output timer. The timer is set in seconds, and the variable memory setup is correct using a word, so the time appears accurately in seconds on the HMI. However, I need to display the time in minutes and seconds (mm:ss). For example, if my timer is 2 minutes and 20 seconds, the display on the actual module shows 2:20, but the HMI only shows 140 seconds. I think one solution is to send two separate values for minutes and seconds, but that's not straightforward. Another approach might be to automatically convert the value within the HMI itself. Thanks.
If you have a timer set to 2 minutes and 20 seconds, the module sends the time value as a total number of seconds to the app.

Yes, the time is transmitted as seconds—140 seconds in both the app and the HMI display. I want to show 2:20 seconds on the HMI interface instead. I tried separating minute and second counters, but since I need a countdown timer, this becomes complicated. If anyone has a suggestion, that would be helpful. Thanks, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulty displaying timer values on the [product_name] app in a familiar minutes:seconds format. The current setup only shows total seconds, making interpretation less intuitive. Users are looking for either automated conversion or a simpler way to show a countdown timer in an easy-to-read format on the HMI.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] app to automatically present timer values in minutes and seconds (mm:ss), just like the display on the [product_name] module, without the need for complex manual workarounds or conversions.
